charts.title: Capital Ratios: CET1, Tier 1 & Total Capital

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

nim.title: Net interest margin and return on assets
nim.content:
NIM is net interest income as a percentage of interest-earning assets. ROA is net income as a percentage of average total assets -- the headline profitability yardstick for a bank's whole balance sheet, not just the loan book.

For Bank of Communications: both have drifted down together -- NIM compression from the PBOC rate-cutting cycle and intensifying mortgage/corporate loan competition has pulled ROA from 0.80% (FY2018-2021) to 0.63% (FY2025), even as the balance sheet keeps growing. A bank can grow assets and still shrink ROA if spreads compress faster than volume grows.

What to watch:

  • Whether NIM stabilises as the rate-cutting cycle matures
  • ROA versus the other large state banks -- BoCom is traditionally the laggard of the "Big Five"
  • Funding cost versus lending yield

capitalRatios.title: Capital ratios: CET1, Tier 1 and total capital
capitalRatios.content:
CET1 (Common Equity Tier 1) is the highest-quality loss-absorbing capital as a percentage of risk-weighted assets; Tier 1 adds other qualifying equity-like instruments (e.g. perpetual capital instruments, preference shares); total capital further adds subordinated (Tier 2) debt. Regulators set minimums on all three.

For Bank of Communications: the FY2025 RMB120bn ordinary-share placement (see the share-issuance chart below) was raised specifically to rebuild CET1 after years of balance-sheet growth had pushed it toward the regulatory floor -- CET1 rose to 11.43% FY2025 from 10.24% FY2024, while Tier 1 only recovered to 12.70% from 12.11% despite the much larger CET1 move, because part of the gap was filled by issuing new ordinary equity rather than hybrid instruments.

What to watch:

  • Whether capital ratios keep rising organically (retained earnings) or need another dilutive raise
  • Risk-weighted asset growth outpacing capital growth
  • Buffer above the regulatory minimum and D-SIB surcharge

shareIssuance.title: Shares outstanding and share issuance
shareIssuance.content:
Shares outstanding is the total ordinary share count; ordinary shares issued (cash) is cash proceeds from new ordinary shares sold in the period, from the financing section of the cash flow statement.

For Bank of Communications: the FY2025 bar is the RMB120bn state-led ordinary-share placement (part of a sector-wide recapitalisation of the large state banks), which increased the share count by roughly 19% -- directly diluting per-share metrics (EPS, book value per share) even though it improved capital ratios. This is the single largest driver of the FY2025 EPS decline relative to net income growth.

What to watch:

  • EPS and BVPS dilution versus the capital-ratio benefit
  • Whether further placements are needed to fund growth or meet rising TLAC/capital requirements
  • Placement price versus book value (dilutive if below NAV per share)

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Bank of Communications Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
